title: Tag Source Data
content_html:
Tag Source Data

Canonical Owners

All four sources live under studio/data/canonical/tags/.

Source Owns Why separate
tag-registry.json flat canonical tag identity, one scalar group, optional exact primary-document override, allowed-group policy classification and primary preference can change without changing tag identity or document membership
tag-aliases.json shorthand keys and canonical tag targets alias curation can evolve independently of canonical identity
tag-assignments.json series tags and nested per-work override deltas assignment state changes independently of vocabulary
tag-groups.json ordered descriptive taxonomy prose explanatory content is not registry or assignment state

The exact schemas and limits are enforced by studio/services/tags/tag_source_model.py; the JSON files are current data, not documentation examples.

Relationship Model

tag-groups descriptions
        |
tag-registry canonical IDs + group + optional primary_document
        ^
tag-aliases shorthand targets
        |
tag-assignments series rows
        -> nested work override deltas
        -> public series/work membership indexes

Analysis Tags document tag_id declarations
        -> private ordered tag-associations.json
        -> Studio read-only document pills

Durable rules:

  • registry IDs are globally unique slug-safe names; each row has exactly one independently validated scalar group;
  • registry rows use tag_registry_v6 and require tag_id, group, and updated_at_utc; they may additionally store one exact Analysis Tags primary_document target and contain no row label, description, or association-membership array;
  • Analysis Tags document front matter owns optional exact tag_id membership. The private docs_tag_associations_v1 product groups valid declarations and orders documents by exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} identity;
  • a missing primary is valid. A stored primary may become unavailable and is retained until another current associated document replaces it or the complete Tag row is deleted; there is no clear-primary mutation;
  • Tag Registry group and document group, title, content, publication, and lifecycle remain independent;
  • aliases and assignments store flat canonical IDs;
  • alias targets must be canonical tags and may not duplicate a registry- resolved group within one alias;
  • a work override belongs under one series row, not in a global work table;
  • effective work tags combine series tags with the override delta;
  • an override that duplicates a series tag is removed during normalization;
  • series/work membership comes from public catalogue indexes and remains externally owned.

Write Boundary

The browser reads and writes through the allowlisted /studio/api/tags/... boundary. Mutation planners validate cross-file effects before studio/services/tags/tag_write_transactions.py atomically replaces one or more canonical files.

tag-groups.json is currently read-only through the app. Registry, aliases, and assignments are writable.

New Tag creates only the Registry row. It does not create a document or an association.

Edit Tag submits the immutable tag_id, accepted scalar group, and only an explicitly changed exact current primary_document. Omitting the primary preserves an existing current or stale value; null is not a clear operation. The editor reads the private association product and cannot search, add, remove, or reorder document membership.

Delete Tag and Demote Tag re-read current Analysis Tags source declarations and are blocked while any document declares the Tag. They never rewrite or delete document source. Conversely, document delete and tag_id assignment, reassignment, or clear rebuild associations without inspecting or mutating the Registry primary.

Change Method

  • vocabulary change: start with Registry/Aliases planners and inspect assignment effects;
  • assignment change: preserve series-first ownership and validate catalogue membership;
  • association change: edit the exact Analysis Tags document declaration and rebuild its private projection; do not mutate membership in Studio;
  • primary change: accept only one exact current association and preserve stale stored identity on unrelated edits;
  • schema change: update loaders, focused mutation paths, migrations, audits, private association consumers, and focused tests;
  • catalogue membership change: use the Studio catalogue synchronization path, then run the narrow consistency check.

Weak Spots

  • cross-file referential integrity is enforced in services/audits rather than by one transactional database;
  • assignment validity depends on generated public catalogue indexes;
  • aliases can preserve historical selection context in assignments, creating a subtle dependency even after canonical IDs are resolved;
  • deleting or disassociating a selected document does not update tag-registry.json; the unavailable primary remains visible until explicit replacement or Tag deletion;
  • the displayed association product is generated, so a source mutation must rebuild it before Studio reflects new membership; primary writes and destructive guards still revalidate current source;
  • Studio has no membership picker, reordering, or bulk association repair UI;
  • hand-editing JSON bypasses planners and transaction safeguards.

Site Consistency Audit is the cross-boundary check. Focused schema behaviour lives in the tag service tests.
